--- lecture: "b" metadata-files: - ../../_slide-settings.yml format: revealjs: theme: default --- ::: {.t-title} ::: {.t-eyebrow} {{< meta course >}} ::: # Writing R Code ::: {.t-rule} ::: ::: {.t-meta} Unit {{< meta unit >}} · Chapter {{< meta chapter >}} · Lecture {{< meta chapter >}}{{< meta lecture >}} ::: ::: {.t-attrib} {{< meta attribution >}} ::: ![]({{< meta unit-art >}}){.t-art} ::: ## Roadmap: Basic Programming ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} 1. Assignment 2. Naming 3. Functions 4. Vectors ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv4 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/map.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: ::: # Assignment ## Assignment {.fs70} ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} - It is often useful to store data in [named objects]{.b .green} - This makes the data easier to use and re-use - This makes the code easier to write and read ::: {.fragment .mt1} - Which command is easier to follow? 1. Dial *7 8 5 8 6 4 0 8 4 1* 2. Call *Office Phone* ::: ::: {.fragment .mt1} - Named objects are created using [assignment]{.b .blue} - Give a **name** then an **arrow** then the **data** ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv5 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/contacts.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: {.fragment} `office <- 7858640841` ::: ::: ::: ## Assigning and Printing ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Store the value 2 under the name x x <- 2 # Typing the name on its own prints the value x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 2 ``` ::: ::: ## Using an Object in Math ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Once x exists, it stands in for its value x * 4 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 8 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Which is the same as writing it out 2 * 4 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 8 ``` ::: ::: ## Updating Requires Assignment ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Using x does not change it x + 1 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # x is still 2 x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 2 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # To update it, assign the result back to the name x <- x + 1 x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ::: ## Using an Object More Than Once ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # x can appear as many times as you like in one line (10 + x - 1) / x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 4 ``` ::: ::: ## Objects Can Create Other Objects ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # The right-hand side can use objects that already exist y <- 10 + x y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 13 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # And a line can use several objects at once y / x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 4.333333 ``` ::: ::: # Naming ## Naming {.fs70} ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} - Object names can [only include]{.b .blue}: - Letters: `a-Z` - Numbers: `0-9` - Underscores: `_` - Periods: `.` ::: {.fragment .mt1} - Additional Rules: - Must [start with a letter or period]{.b .blue} - Cannot contain spaces or dashes - Cannot contain other symbols - Names are case-sensitive (`age` ≠ `Age`) ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv5 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/business_card.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: ::: ## Good Names are a Balancing Act ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- 93 # legal, but what is it? rate <- 93 # too short to be clear heart_rate_in_beats_per_minute <- 93 # too long to type heart_rate_bpm <- 93 # just right ``` ::: ## Pitfall: No Spaces or Dashes ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="false"} heart rate <- 93 # Error: unexpected symbol heart-rate <- 93 # R reads this as heart - rate, not a name ``` ::: ::: aside *Note.* These will not even run --- R cannot make sense of the line at all. Use an underscore instead: `heart_rate`. ::: ## Pitfall: No Special Symbols ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="false"} age@time2 <- 12 # Error: @ means something else in R ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} age_time2 <- 12 # correct age_time2 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 12 ``` ::: ::: ## Pitfall: Cannot Start with a Number or Underscore ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="false"} 1_heart_rate <- 93 # Error: unexpected input _heart_rate <- 93 # Error: unexpected input ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} heart_rate_1 <- 93 # correct: the digit comes last heart_rate_1 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 93 ``` ::: ::: ## Names are Case-Sensitive ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} heart_rate <- 93 Heart_rate <- 88 # These are two entirely different objects heart_rate ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 93 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} Heart_rate ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 88 ``` ::: ::: # Functions ## Functions {.fs70} ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} - [Recipes]{.b .green} allow chefs to cook up tasty treats - Recipes call for ingredients - Recipes involve one or more steps - Steps transform ingredients into treats ::: {.fragment .mt1} - [Functions]{.b .blue} are like *customizable* recipes - Functions call for inputs ("arguments") - Functions involve one or more lines of code - Code transforms inputs into outputs - Using functions requires parentheses (usually) ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv5 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/blender.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: {.fragment} `out <- f(in1, in2)` ::: ::: ::: ## Functions Do a Task More Readably ::: {.f5} `output <- function_name(input)` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # The hard way 9 ^ (1 / 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # The readable way x <- sqrt(9) x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ::: ## Functions Can Transform Objects ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} y <- 9 # The input can be an object rather than a literal value sqrt(y) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 3 ``` ::: ::: ## Functions Can Transform Calculations ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} 2 / 3 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.6666667 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # The input can also be the result of a calculation round(2 / 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1 ``` ::: ::: ## Arguments Customize a Function ::: {.f5} `output <- function_name(argument, argument_name = argument_value)` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} round(2 / 3, digits = 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.67 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} round(2 / 3, digits = 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.667 ``` ::: ::: ## Some Arguments Have Defaults ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # digits has a default value of 0, so this... round(2 / 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # ...means exactly the same thing as this round(2 / 3, digits = 0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1 ``` ::: ::: # Vectors ## Vectors {.fs70} ::: {.columns .pv4} ::: {.column width="60%"} - [Vectors]{.b .blue} combine similar objects into a collection - *I like to imagine a train pulling multiple cars*
![](../../img/traincar.png) - A vector is one object with many sub-objects - We refer to each sub-object as an [element]{.b .green} ::: {.fragment .mt1} - Some functions [transform each element]{.b .green} in turn - *Double the amount of cargo in every train car* ::: ::: {.fragment .mt1} - Some functions [summarize across elements]{.b .green} - *Calculate the total cargo across all train cars* ::: ::: ::: {.column .tc .pv5 width="40%"} {{< lif "../../icons/old_train.json" trigger=hover colors=secondary:#2a76dd class=rc >}} ::: {.fragment} `v <- c(1, 2, 3)` ::: ::: ::: ## Combining Elements into a Vector ::: {.f5} `vector_name <- c(element1, element2, element3)` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="false"} x <- 4 9 16 25 # Error: you must separate elements with commas ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- c(4, 9, 16, 25) x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 4 9 16 25 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} y <- c(2, 3) y ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 2 3 ``` ::: ::: ## Combining Vectors and Elements ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # c() also joins whole vectors together c(x, y) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 4 9 16 25 2 3 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # And vectors and single elements c(x, y, 20) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 4 9 16 25 2 3 20 ``` ::: ::: ## Math Transforms Each Element ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} x + 1 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 5 10 17 26 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} x * 3 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 12 27 48 75 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # But as before, nothing is saved without assignment x ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 4 9 16 25 ``` ::: ::: ## Some Functions Transform Each Element ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} sqrt(x) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 2 3 4 5 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} log(x) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 1.386294 2.197225 2.772589 3.218876 ``` ::: ::: ## Other Functions Summarize the Whole Vector ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} length(x) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 4 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} sum(x) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 54 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} mean(x) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 13.5 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} average(x) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` Error in `average()`: ! could not find function "average" ``` ::: ::: ## Pitfall: Missing Values are Contagious ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} scores <- c(10, 12, 20, NA, 8) # NA spreads: the mean depends on the value we do not have mean(scores) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] NA ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} # Ask for the mean of the non-missing values instead mean(scores, na.rm = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 12.5 ``` ::: :::

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
